::: notes
"A stud is a promise. A brick from 1958 still clicks into a brick from today."

1:00.

Let the bricks seat before you speak. This is agreement, not argument, so keep it brisk. Say it, don't show it: "Imagine every set with its own stud size. That's the drawer of travel adapters anyone who has plugged in a laptop in Europe owns." Without the shared standard there is no system, just a pile of incompatible toys.

Click: "Pharma already has its stud." The brick hops from org A and clicks onto org B.

"Imagine this work without CDISC: not even between companies, just between two teams in the same building." Ask it as a real question and let it hang.

What the stud buys: a shared language, tooling that composes, a workforce whose skills transfer.

Transition: "And we don't just exchange data. We build it like a product."
:::
